Advances: M3 replay validation ritual (ancora-yzu.19)

The authorized M3 replay on Ancora 1.0.0-rc.1 crashed in Ancora.Derive.Resolver.walk/2 because Enum received nil. This prevented Atlas PR 144 from producing JSON and made all three gate benchmark samples measure crash-to-exit time. Reproduce with the selection and benchmark commands in scripts/replay/SELECTION.md and bench/gate_bench.exs. Full evidence: /Users/mz/.local/state/agentic-runs/ancora/ancora-yzu.19/codex-yzu19-impl-1/m3-replay-results.md.

Acceptance: spec.check completes on Atlas PR 144 and the pinned benchmark commit, the replay case emits a derived/drift finding naming Atlas.Slack.KnowledgeCapture.handle_message_action/2, and the benchmark measures completed gates. Do not weaken or tune the detector to satisfy the replay bar.

Repro: Crash confirmed at 341c270 before the fix. After the fix, Atlas PR 144 completed through a normal JSON verdict, and all three pinned benchmark gates completed with median 33719.7 ms instead of crashing. The requested derived/drift finding for Atlas.Slack.KnowledgeCapture.handle_message_action/2 was absent because that public clause is canonically identical across the PR; the PR changes private do_handle_message_action/2. Follow-up: [Replace invalid Atlas PR 144 replay drift fixture](https://github.com/iautom8things/ancora/blob/beadwork/issues/ancora-yzu.34.json).
Root cause: Atlas binds a local variable named quote in create_slack_source!/0. Code.string_to_quoted represents each reference as {:quote, metadata, nil}; Resolver.walk/2 matched that variable as the quote special form and sent its nil context to walk_call_arguments/2, which calls Enum.reduce/3.

Summary: The quote-special-form walk clause now accepts only list arguments, so quote variables fall through to the existing variable clause while real quote bodies retain the same traversal. The regression test proved red before the fix and asserts the resolver still records Foo.Bar.run/1 after walking quote variables, guarding against a crash-only fix that drops resolvable calls. I checked every epic lesson against the diff; none required another code or test change.

SELECTION.md:29 already excludes this fan-out class by design. ancora-yzu.34 tracks the fixture replacement.
- Bench completion: 3 runs, 28942.9 / 29214.3 / 29165.1 ms, median 29165.1, no crash, exit 0. SEAM: bench/gate_bench.exs:68 accepts status in [0, 1], and a resolver crash inside spec.check also exits 1 -- I proved that directly (see mutation proofs), so the bench alone cannot distinguish crash from fail verdict. Corroborated by running the bench's exact inner command at HEAD: MIX_ENV=dev mix spec.check --root <clone> --base 4f6c0760^ produced a 383-line report ending in "spec.check result=fail tier=branch errors=63 warnings=314". Real gate work, not crash-to-exit.
- Mutation proofs:
  * Revert lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex to c9d1efe -> RED, and only the new test failed (1 of 32): Protocol.UndefinedError, "Enumerable not implemented for type Atom", got value nil, at lib/ancora/derive/resolver.ex:145 via resolve/3. Exact root cause confirmed.

Disclosing this rather than counting it -- that mutation is undetectable by construction, for any test.

It resolves "quote do\n  unquote(module).run(:ok)\nend" and asserts the dynamic_module entry, so any break in quote-body traversal turns result.unresolved into []. Verified RED under the swallow-everything mutation. Not a Gap.
- Intent-level scope concerns: none. I enumerated the real quote special forms through Code.string_to_quoted -- "quote do ... end", "quote(do: ...)", "quote bind_quoted: [...] do", "quote location: :keep, generated: true do", "quote unquote: false do" -- and every one carries list args, so every input that resolved before still takes the identical path. The only shape newly diverted is {:quote, meta, nil}/{:quote, meta, atom}, the local-variable shape, which previously raised rather than resolving. The change strictly adds tolerance; it removes nothing.

Verdict: PASS

Notes (advisory only):
- The IMPLEMENTED record's root-cause sentence names do_handle_message_action/2 as the changed private function. It is not changed; resolve_and_prompt/3 and extract_message_action/1 are. The conclusion the ticket rests on is unaffected and in fact better supported.
- Spec gap, not a code gap: no must in ancora.derive.spec.md states that the resolver tolerates a well-parsed node whose children field is not a list. The behavior is covered only transitively through qualified_call_disposition's tag; parse_degrades_to_finding covers unparseable sources, which this is not. A future contributor has no spec sentence to point at. Worth a sentence in qualified_call_disposition or a sibling requirement when the spec is next opened.
- bench/gate_bench.exs:68 treats exit 1 as success. Since a detector crash also exits 1, the benchmark cannot detect the very regression this ticket fixed. Worth tightening to check for the verdict line in stdout. Out of scope here.

Fixture honesty: confirmed by parsing the fixture with Code.string_to_quoted. It yields three {:quote, _, nil} nodes; the def-head param is skipped by the definition clause, but the `quote = nil` LHS (via the := call-argument walk) and the Foo.Bar.run(quote) argument (via walk_terms) both reach the walk, so the crash shape is exercised twice on real paths.

Mutation bite: all three mutations run against test/ancora/derive/resolver_test.exs:146, worktree restored after each.
(a) reverted guard (removed `when is_list(args)`) -> red, Enumerable-nil crash in walk/2, the original bug.
(b) lazy fix (no guard, walk wrapped in try/rescue returning pre-walk state) -> red on `calls == MapSet.new([{Foo.Bar, :run, 1}])` (got empty set). The hide-calls assertion is live.
(c) misclassify {:quote, _, nil} as add_unresolved(:dynamic_module, ...) -> red on `unresolved == []`.

Convention: matches the file. Name states precondition and outcome, uses the shared setup_all ctx, resolve!/2 helper, heredoc source, and the same MapSet equality assertions as neighbors. Placed adjacent to the existing quote/unquote test.

Sibling shapes: none remain. Audit of every walk clause admitting a nil third element, verified by running each special-form name as a variable (def run(name); name = nil; Foo.Bar.run(name)) through Resolver.resolve at HEAD: quote, unquote, super, apply, __CALLER__ fall through guarded clauses (resolver.ex:197, 203, 219) to the variable clause at resolver.ex:224; alias/require match resolver.ex:149 with nil args but add_aliases/3's catch-all (resolver.ex:433) absorbs nil; import/use hit resolver.ex:160-161 and return state. In every case {Foo.Bar, :run, 1} still resolves. __block__ and __aliases__ (the only other clauses that would crash on nil, resolver.ex:122-123) are reserved tokens - string_to_quoted rejects them, so those shapes are unreachable from parsed source. The single-shape test is sufficient because quote was the only reachable member of the crash class.

Spec tag: ancora.derive.qualified_call_disposition is a fair binding. The requirement says a member-qualified call shall enter the call set as {Mod, :f, arity}; mutation (b) drops exactly that mechanism and the test goes red, so the tag is not vacuous. The crash-tolerance aspect has no dedicated requirement id, but of the existing ids this is the honest one.

Verdict: PASS
Notes: advisory only - a variable named alias/require/import/use is swallowed by the ignored-form clauses rather than the variable clause. Behaviorally identical today (state returned unchanged, calls preserved, proven by the probe), just worth knowing those clauses shadow the variable clause.
